articles.title: Emma Watson donated $1 million to a UK fund fighting sexual harassment; its impact report later recorded 46,100 women and girls reached, over 20,000 professionals trained and 59 grants awarded
articles.summary: Emma Watson’s contribution to the fight against sexual harassment in the UK has helped support a network of organisations working with survivors and
articles.body: Emma Watson’s contribution to the fight against sexual harassment in the UK has helped support a network of organisations working with survivors and campaigning for safer workplaces and communities. A new impact report by Rosa, the UK Fund for Women and Girls, has detailed the work carried out through the Justice and Equality Fund, which was launched in 2018 following the global #MeToo movement. According to the same report, published on March 5, 2025, the initiative reached 46,100 women and girls, trained more than 20,000 professionals and distributed nearly £2.54 million through 59 grants. The fund’s launch and Watson’s contribution were also reported by Sky News and The Guardian. The Justice and Equality Fund was established in collaboration with TIME’S UP UK to address sexual harassment, abuse and the culture of impunity surrounding them. More than 400 donors contributed a combined £2.9 million, including Watson, who donated $1 million, and Comic Relief, which contributed £1 million.The money was distributed across three programmes designed to support survivors, strengthen women’s organisations and encourage wider social change. Grants ranged from £2,000 to £200,000, with funding reaching both established charities and smaller grassroots organisations working across different parts of the UK.One of the major outcomes was the establishment of a specialist legal advice service for women experiencing sexual harassment at work. The service helped women across England and Wales access legal guidance and understand the options available to them. The fund also supported initiatives aimed at improving how institutions respond to sexual harassment. More than 9,000 police professionals received awareness training, while other projects focused on tackling sexual misconduct in universities and improving support for survivors.Among its other achievements was the establishment of Northern Ireland’s first rape crisis service in more than a decade. Funding also helped develop a resource hub for university students and staff, offering guidance on preventing and addressing sexual misconduct in higher education.The initiative further supported campaigns led by young people and local organisations. The Compass Centre in Shetland, for instance, used the funding to encourage young residents to challenge gender-based violence in their communities. Its work included campaigns that attracted national media attention and partnerships with local organisations. The centre also reported a 90% increase in the number of people approaching it for support, rising from 51 to 97.The fund’s work extended beyond providing direct assistance to survivors. It also contributed to efforts aimed at changing workplace policies and strengthening legal protections. One significant development highlighted in the report was the introduction of a legal duty requiring employers to take reasonable steps to prevent sexual harassment at work.The Worker Protection (Amendment of Equality Act 2010) Act 2023 received Royal Assent in October 2023 and came into force on October 26, 2024. It introduced a preventative duty for employers, making workplace sexual harassment prevention a legal responsibility rather than leaving organisations to respond only after incidents occur.The report also highlights the importance of collaboration between organisations working on women’s rights. By bringing together charities, legal experts, businesses, trade unions, schools and campaigners, the fund helped create partnerships that could continue beyond individual funding programmes. However, the report points out that the need for sustained support remains considerable. Despite the progress made, women and girls continue to experience sexual harassment and abuse across workplaces, educational institutions and public spaces. Organisations working on the frontline also continue to face funding challenges.The Justice and Equality Fund demonstrates how financial support can help smaller organisations expand their reach while contributing to broader institutional change. Its findings also underline the importance of continuing to invest in organisations supporting women and girls, particularly those working directly with survivors of abuse.You use AI every day. articles.title: Elephant calf airlifted from Keralam to Vantara for life-saving treatment
articles.summary: Maya, an elephant calf found alone as a newborn on a riverbank 18 months ago, was airlifted from Keralam to Vantara's hospital in Jamnagar on Nov 5, after
articles.body: Maya, an elephant calf found alone as a newborn on a riverbank 18 months ago, was airlifted from Keralam to Vantara's hospital in Jamnagar on Nov 5, after fractures in both front legs left her unable to stand.Acting on an initiative by RIL exec director and Vantara founder Anant Ambani, the organisation deployed a specialised veterinary team following a transfer order from Keralam's chief wildlife warden, P Pugazhendi.Found near Kaprikkad on Apr 19, 2025, the weak, dehydrated newborn had not received her mother's milk and couldn't even suckle. Assistant forest veterinary officer Binoy Babu and caregivers fed and nursed her for over a year.In July 2026, Maya slipped while playing and injured her shoulder. Despite physiotherapy, splints & supplements, her bones became increasingly fragile. By Oct, she had front-leg fractures, a chest infection and pressure sores. Her prognosis was grave.After Kerala's chief wildlife warden sought wider expert opinion, Vantara veterinary adviser Kushal Konwar Sarma identified a possible parathyroid-related disorder that may respond to treatment. Yaduraj Khadpekar, head veterinarian at Vantara's Elephant Care Centre, concurred, and the medical board unanimously agreed.Maya travelled by a life-support airlift, accompanied by three Vantara elephant veterinarians, paravets and caregivers, along with Binoy C Babu and her familiar caregiver, Nikhil Babu. She will receive round-the-clock monitoring, pain management, advanced diagnostics, hydraulic lifting support and hydrotherapy where appropriate. Vantara - a global wildlife rescue, care, welfare and conservation initiative based in Jamnagar - will facilitate her return to Abhayaranyam after treatment.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: Leaders of four nations meet in Manila after two-year gapNEW DELHI: Reflecting Beijing's long-standing opposition to Quad, the Chinese state-backed media has dismissed the upcoming leaders' summit in Manila as a hasty geopolitical manoeuvre and warned against internationalising the South China Sea disputes. The leaders of India, Japan, Australia and US are expected to meet on the margins of the Asean summit starting Nov 16 for what will be the first such meeting in two years.While an official announcement about Quad leaders' summit is still awaited, US secretary of state Marco Rubio has said the leaders of the grouping will meet in the Philippines. Significantly, President Donald Trump is scheduled to travel to China from Manila for the Apec summit.An opinion piece in Global Times said, "this small circle, which had been dormant for two years, has finally been dusted off and brought back from the freezer by the US administration". "If certain countries seek to use a small-circle summit to openly demonstrate their intention to interfere in South China Sea affairs, China will inevitably oppose it resolutely," it said.The leaders' summit takes place amid renewed China-Philippines maritime tensions, allowing the US to reinforce its continued presence in the region. Both Beijing and Moscow see Quad as a China containment alliance.This will be the first Quad leaders' summit since PM Modi's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Kazan in 2024 that opened the door for normalisation of Sino-Indian ties. India sees Quad as an initiative based on democratic values and respect for rule of law that is working towards a free, inclusive and prosperous Indo-Pacific region.The Global Times piece also said India's approach bears clear hallmarks of balance-of-power manoeuvring."New Delhi is unwilling to jeopardise improving the China-India relationship by aligning with other nations' efforts to contain China, nor is it willing to make unilateral concessions on trade tariffs and market access," it said.The same view was expressed by a Global Times editorial that said India emphasises strategic autonomy and hopes to use multilateral cooperation to create opportunities for industrial development, rather than "simply fall in line with an economic containment strategy against China designed by other countries".You use AI every day. articles.title: Congress donations plunge 75% to Rs 131 cr, lowest in 3 years
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Contributions received by the Congress in excess of Rs 20,000 totalled Rs 130.7 crore in 2025-26, which is barely one-fourth of its Rs 517.4
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Contributions received by the Congress in excess of Rs 20,000 totalled Rs 130.7 crore in 2025-26, which is barely one-fourth of its Rs 517.4 crore donation receipts in 2024-25.As per the 2025-26 contribution report of the Congress filed with EC, Prudent Electoral Trust contributed 19% of Congress's total donation kitty in the relevant year. In 2024-25, Prudent had accounted for 41.8% of contributions received by Congress.Prudent is the only electoral trust through which donations, largely corporate, were routed to Congress last year. At Rs 25 crore, the trust's contributions to the party, however, were only 11.5% of the Rs 216 crore funds it had channelled to the party in 2024-25.The steep 75% decline in Congress's total contributions in excess of Rs 20,000, compared with 2024-25, could be due to several factors. Given that 2024-25 was the general election year, a marked rise (84% as compared to 2023-24) in contributions to the main opposition party was on expected lines. What is interesting though is that the Rs 130.7 crore contribution receipts in 2025-26 are nearly 53% less than the amount it had received even in 2023-24.The steep decline was witnessed despite 2025-26 being the year of Bihar assembly elections and the run-up to elections in Assam, Keralam, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry held in April 2026.The Congress audit report for 2025-26, which is not available yet, will throw light on the party's other sources of funding. In 2024-25, Congress's collection from the issuance and sale of coupons was over Rs 350 crore.Among the key contributors last year, other than Prudent, were Star Cement Ltd (Rs 5 crore), Sajjan Bhajanka (Rs 4 crore), Afnan Constructions (Rs 3 crore), Prem Kumar Bhajanka (Rs 2 crore) and IPSUM Proadvisors and SMS Builders (Rs 1 crore each).Just nine contributions of Rs 1 crore or more accounted for Rs 43 crore, or nearly one-third of the party's total receipts. In comparison, 1,321 contributions of Rs 5 lakh or less together added up to Rs 37.2 crore, accounting for just 28.5% of the total. The median contribution among the 1,735 entries was Rs 3 lakh, highlighting how a relatively small number of large donations accounted for a substantial share of the party's funding.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: The event in Bridgwater, Somerset, attracted people from all over the country to watch.
articles.body:
Rock shows, Del Boy and his three-wheeler from Only Fools and Horses, and a circus big top were among the themes showcased during a spectacular illuminated carnival procession.

Thousands of people watched the event in Bridgwater, Somerset, where clubs spend the entire year preparing carts for the show.

Dan Prosser from the Renegades Carnival Club said the preparations were "more like a lifestyle than just a hobby," adding his non-carnival friends think his devotion to the event is "absolutely nuts".

The carnival ended with 210 people - including local MP Sir Ashley Fox - taking part in squibbing, where a large firework, strapped to a solid block of wood on the end of a pole, is lit.

articles.title: A stolen car left him with devastating leg injuries at 18, and he spent six months in a wheelchair; decades later, he deadlifted 285 kg and became a world-record powerlifter
articles.summary: An Irish powerlifter who suffered devastating leg injuries after being struck by a stolen car at 18 has turned a life-changing accident into an
articles.body: An Irish powerlifter who suffered devastating leg injuries after being struck by a stolen car at 18 has turned a life-changing accident into an extraordinary sporting achievement. Liam Beville spent 6 months in a wheelchair, underwent multiple surgeries and had to learn to walk again. Decades later, he lifted 285 kg to establish a Guinness World Records title, competing against able-bodied athletes despite his long-term disability. His journey from rehabilitation to international recognition has now inspired an autobiography, in which he recounts the determination, setbacks and years of training behind his record-breaking achievement.Liam Beville overcame devastating injuries to become a world-record powerlifterBeville's life changed on 3 June 1983, when he was struck by a stolen car in a head-on collision while walking along a footpath in Limerick, Ireland. According to Guinness World Records, the crash left both his legs catastrophically injured, with open compound fractures, extensive trauma and lasting structural damage.The injuries required extensive medical treatment and a prolonged recovery. Beville spent a year in plaster casts, six months in a wheelchair and underwent multiple operations. He also needed a hip replacement and a full knee replacement, consequences that continued to affect him long after the initial accident.His recovery involved learning how to walk again, a challenge that required patience and considerable physical effort. Friends helped him during the difficult period, even pushing him around in a pram while his legs healed.Weight training became the foundation of his recoveryBeville initially entered the gym as part of his rehabilitation while still relying on crutches. What began as an effort to rebuild his strength gradually developed into a lasting passion for weight training.The Guinness World Records explains that he began lifting weights after the accident and soon discovered an interest in powerlifting. His progress was remarkably quick considering the severity of his injuries.Just three years after the crash, he won the Limerick Powerlifting Championships and received the Best Lifter award. His early success demonstrated that his rehabilitation had developed into something much more than a recovery programme.In 1988, he broke his first national deadlift record. Four years later, he broke the Irish Powerlifting total record and established Irish and Celtic Nations deadlift records.These achievements marked the beginning of a competitive career that would continue for decades. Beville also worked in technology before retiring because of his disability and later developed a successful self-taught business in web development and digital marketing.What made his 285 kg deadlift a historic achievementBeville's most remarkable achievement came on 5 February 2022, when he was 57 years old. At the IrishPO National Single Lift Championships in Limerick, he lifted 285 kg, equivalent to 628.31 lb, to establish the Guinness World Records title for the heaviest deadlift by a male athlete in the MP4 impairment classification.The weight was comparable to an adult male alligator, a vending machine or a baby grand piano. Guinness World Records confirmed the achievement in its July 2025 article, describing how Beville had worked towards the lift for approximately three years.The MP4 classification refers to an impairment affecting the ability to generate full force for movement through the arms and legs. Despite his disability, Beville had always competed in mainstream powerlifting competitions rather than entering a separate disabled category.At the event where he established the record, he was the only disabled participant. Organisers also presented him with the Best Lifter award, recognising his performance among the competitors.Years of training helped him compete on his own termsBeville's record was not the result of a sudden breakthrough. His preparation involved training independently, using box squats, resistance bands and carefully planned deadlift cycles to gradually build strength.According to Guinness World Records, it took him around three years to reach the weight required for his world record. The accident left him with physical limitations, but he didn’t lower his expectations, instead continued pursuing his ambition.His decision to compete against able-bodied athletes was also central to his approach. Beville wanted his performances to be judged on their merits and believed that achievements should not be dismissed because of disability.His sporting career also extended beyond the single record. According to a report by Guinness World Records, by July 2026 Beville had broken multiple records in 4 different weight divisions in powerlifting, and was number 1 in the world in his age and weight category.The report also noted that 2026 marked 40 years since he first competed in a mainstream powerlifting competition.His autobiography brings decades of determination to a wider audienceBeville’s story has now moved beyond sporting competitions with his autobiography, Unbroken – The Liam Beville Story. The 61-year-old wrote the book to document his journey from the devastating accident to becoming a record-breaking powerlifter, Guinness World Records said.His journey has also been recognised beyond the sporting world. The former President of Ireland, Michael D. Higgins, praised Beville’s strength and bravery in a letter to Guinness World Records.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has ordered the Department of Justice (DOJ) to immediately investigate Democratic lawmakers, accusing them of threatening senior
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has ordered the Department of Justice (DOJ) to immediately investigate Democratic lawmakers, accusing them of threatening senior administration officials, Republican donors and political supporters with impeachment, prosecution and imprisonment. Trump described the alleged actions as “extortion at the highest level” and called for those responsible to be held accountable.In a lengthy statement on his social media platform Truth Social, Trump claimed that Democratic leaders were threatening officials, including the US attorney general, with impeachment despite allegedly having no grounds to pursue such action.“The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people, including the Attorney General of the United States, and others, with Impeachment and many other forms of punishment, even though they admit they have no reason to do so, and there have been no impeachable acts committed, or even thought of, by the victims of this illegal process,” Trump wrote.“This is extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable for this,” he added.The US president also alleged that Republican donors were being targeted because of their political affiliations, claiming that prominent financial supporters faced threats of imprisonment and other penalties.“Also, they’re threatening our Donors, some of the most respected people anywhere in the World, with imprisonment, and many other levels of punishment, just because they happen to be Republicans, or Republican supporters. This is Weaponization and Lawfare at another level,” Trump said.Trump separately singled out Michigan Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin, alleging that she was seeking action against young people who support Republican values.“The Senator from Michigan, Elissa Slotkin, is saying that she is going to go after all young people that believe in Republican Values, and that give even the slightest inclination to be a Republican,” he wrote.Escalating his criticism, Trump alleged that Democratic political leaders had sent threatening letters to people he described as innocent. He subsequently issued a direct instruction to federal law enforcement.“Threatening letters have been sent to many people, all innocent, from Democrat Political Leaders. By copy of this statement, I am ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately!” he declared.In a second Truth Social post, Trump doubled down on his allegations against Democratic lawmakers, calling them “SLEAZEBAGS” and demanding that they face imprisonment.Trump wrote, "These SLEAZEBAGS should go to jail for what they are doing. The Senate must act, and stop being pushed around to the point of the Republican Party losing Elections, and worse!"The order comes against the backdrop of a changed political landscape following the midterm elections, in which Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress. The shift is expected to expand Democratic lawmakers' ability to conduct oversight hearings, issue subpoenas and investigate administration decisions.The political confrontation also coincides with a leadership transition at the White House. On November 7, Trump announced that Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff from November 9, while Wiles would move to the Trump Political Operation.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2003, Goldie Hawn started a programme to help children manage stress and understand emotions; 23 years later, MindUP reports reaching more than 7 million children across 48 countries through brain-based lessons
articles.summary: Children learn mathematics, science and languages in school, but understanding their own emotions and managing stress can be equally important to their
articles.body: Children learn mathematics, science and languages in school, but understanding their own emotions and managing stress can be equally important to their development. Recognising this need, actor Goldie Hawn established the Goldie Hawn Foundation in 2003 to help children develop emotional awareness and mental well-being. The initiative led to the creation of MindUP, a school-based programme that combines neuroscience, mindfulness and social-emotional learning to give children practical tools for handling everyday challenges.According to the Stavros Niarchos Foundation (SNF) Global Health Initiative, which supports MindUP, the programme has worked with children in 48 countries since its establishment in 2003. A February 13, 2026, profile published by ASU+GSV Summit reported that MindUP had reached more than 7 million children worldwide. Developed with neuroscientists, educators, psychologists and researchers, its curriculum aims to help children understand how their brains work, regulate emotions, reduce stress and build empathy. The initiative has grown from an effort to improve children's emotional well-being into an international education programme.How Goldie Hawn developed the initiativeHawn established the Goldie Hawn Foundation after becoming concerned about rising school violence, youth depression and suicide, as well as the difficulties children faced in managing increasingly stressful lives. She believed that schools needed to teach children more than traditional academic subjects and should also help them understand their emotions and mental health.To develop a practical approach, the foundation collaborated with neuroscientists, educators, psychologists and researchers. Their work resulted in MindUP, an evidence-based curriculum designed to introduce children to brain science and teach them skills for emotional regulation and positive behaviour.The programme was developed around the understanding that children who recognise their emotions and learn how their brains respond to stress can become better equipped to handle difficult situations. Rather than treating emotional well-being as a separate subject, MindUP integrates these lessons into classroom activities and everyday learning.What children learn through MindUPMindUP is designed for children aged 3 to 14 and also provides resources and guidance for educators and parents. Its curriculum brings together four key areas: neuroscience, social-emotional learning, positive psychology and mindful awareness. One of its central elements is helping children understand the brain and how it responds to different emotions and experiences. By learning about brain functions, children can better recognise what happens when they feel frightened, angry, anxious or overwhelmed.The programme also uses short mindfulness exercises, including breathing activities and brain breaks, to help students pause, focus their attention and manage stress. These practices are intended to help children become more aware of their thoughts and feelings rather than reacting immediately to difficult situations. Another important component is empathy. Through classroom discussions and activities, students learn to understand other people's feelings, develop positive relationships and respond to situations with kindness and compassion. The lessons also encourage optimism, resilience and responsible decision-making.The curriculum is organised into four interconnected units that gradually develop children's awareness, self-regulation and social skills. According to the SNF Global Health Initiative, these lessons aim to strengthen prosocial behaviour, executive functioning and social and emotional competence.From classrooms to an international programmeOver the years, MindUP has expanded beyond its initial school-based activities. Its resources are now available through an interactive online learning platform, allowing educators and families to access its lessons and practices in different settings. The programme has also received support from organisations working in education and mental health. The Stavros Niarchos Foundation Global Health Initiative supports MindUP in making its curriculum more accessible, including through an animated version of its first unit, Understanding the Brain. The initiative is intended to make the lessons more engaging and accessible to children.Its international reach has also increased significantly. The February 2026 ASU+GSV Summit profile reported that MindUP had reached more than 7 million children across 48 countries. The programme's expansion reflects growing interest in social-emotional learning and the importance of addressing children's mental well-being as part of their education. MindUP's approach also highlights the role teachers and parents play in supporting children's emotional development. By using similar techniques at school and at home, adults can help children practise self-awareness, manage difficult feelings and develop healthier relationships.More than two decades after Hawn established her foundation, MindUP continues to focus on a simple idea: children need the skills to understand their minds and emotions just as much as they need academic knowledge. Its international growth demonstrates how brain science and practical classroom lessons can be brought together to support children's emotional development, resilience and overall well-being.You use AI every day. articles.title: Iran's IRGC claims self-imposed 2,000-km ballistic missile range limit 'has been lifted'
articles.summary: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has announced that a self-imposed restriction limiting the range of its ballistic missiles to 2,000
articles.body: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has announced that a self-imposed restriction limiting the range of its ballistic missiles to 2,000 kilometres (1,200 miles) “has been lifted”. The move could open the door for Tehran to pursue longer-range missile capabilities amid growing fears of a renewed full-scale conflict with the United States and Israel.According to news agency AP, IRGC spokesman general Hossein Mohebbi made the remarks at a press conference in Tehran on Saturday. Asked whether the restriction on missile range remained in place, Mohebbi said, “That restriction has been lifted for us.”He added that Iran would demonstrate its capabilities rather than make further statements. “We will demonstrate these capabilities in practice,” he said, according to reports.The announcement came days after a statement attributed to Iran’s Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khomeini, warned that “any kind and level of threat” from the US or Israel would be met with a response without geographical limits.The 2,000-kilometre range had placed parts of Greece and the Balkans, the entire Arabian Peninsula, the Levant and most of Egypt within the reach of Iran’s ballistic missiles, according to The Times of Israel.However, Mohebbi did not say whether Iran currently possesses missiles capable of travelling beyond that distance. Iran is not known to have operational ballistic missiles with a range exceeding 2,000 kilometres.US officials have previously warned that technology developed through Iran’s space programme could potentially be repurposed to build intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs). In March, Iran reportedly attempted, but failed, to strike the joint US-UK military base at Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean, approximately 4,000 kilometres (2,500 miles) away, The Times of Israel reported.The missile announcement comes as military tensions continue across the region. The US Central Command said on Saturday that American forces had disabled a St Kitts-flagged commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman after it allegedly ignored repeated warnings and attempted to leave the region after visiting an Iranian port.The US has been enforcing a naval blockade on Iran around the Strait of Hormuz, a key global shipping route. Tehran, meanwhile, has maintained pressure on the waterway and claimed attacks on tankers. The Iranian military said on Saturday that two tankers had struck mines and caught fire in the area.Separately, NBC News reported that some of US President Donald Trump’s advisers had told him, five days before Tuesday’s midterm elections, that any decision to resume major combat operations against Iran should be taken before the new Congress is sworn in in January.The IRGC’s announcement does not establish that Iran has already developed longer-range missiles.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Four of six endangered broad-headed snakes released into the Australian wild have survived their first few months in a world-first conservation experiment
articles.body: Four of six endangered broad-headed snakes released into the Australian wild have survived their first few months in a world-first conservation experiment that could offer a new approach to protecting threatened reptiles. The juvenile snakes were bred in captivity and released in May 2026 into restored rocky habitat in the Shoalhaven region of New South Wales. Conservationists used specially designed artificial rocks to recreate the natural shelters the reptiles depend on for protection, temperature regulation and hunting. Researchers from the University of Technology Sydney (UTS), working with conservation organisation Aussie Ark and Indigenous rangers, have been monitoring the animals through regular field surveys. The latest update, released on November 6, reported that at least four of the six snakes were still alive.Australia's endangered broad-headed snake faces mounting threatsThe broad-headed snake (Hoplocephalus bungaroides) is an endangered reptile endemic to Australia. Recognisable by its black body, yellow bands and flattened head, it is primarily found in sandstone habitats across the Sydney Basin and surrounding areas of New South Wales.These snakes depend heavily on natural rock formations, particularly sandstone crevices, where they shelter during the day, regulate their body temperature and find protection from predators. They emerge mainly at night to hunt smaller reptiles, including geckos and skinks.However, the destruction and removal of natural bush rocks have significantly reduced suitable habitat. Habitat fragmentation, illegal collection, drought and bushfires have added to the pressures facing the species. The loss of suitable rocky shelters is particularly damaging because these structures provide several essential resources within a relatively small area.Drought and bushfires contributed to a sharp population declineLong-term research led by University of Technology Sydney wildlife ecologist Professor Jonathan Webb has documented the pressures affecting the species. His monitoring work recorded a significant population decline following the 2017–19 drought and the devastating Australian bushfires of 2019–20.According to UTS, the monitored population had declined by approximately 64% by 2023. Researchers also recorded little breeding activity during the three years following the bushfires, raising concerns about the species' ability to recover.Broad-headed snakes have a relatively slow reproductive cycle, making population recovery difficult. Females generally reproduce every two or three years, while young snakes can take around five years to reach adulthood. Consequently, the loss of breeding animals and suitable habitat can have long-lasting effects on local populations.Conservationists breed endangered snakes in captivityThe reintroduction programme began in October 2024, when Aussie Ark secured 17 adult broad-headed snakes from the wild to establish a captive breeding population. Three additional adults joined the programme the following month, bringing the founding group to 20.The animals were housed at Conservation Ark, Aussie Ark's conservation facility in Somersby, New South Wales. The organisation subsequently achieved successful captive breeding using the wild-sourced founders, producing eight juvenile snakes.Six of these juveniles were selected for the experimental release in May 2026, while two remained in captivity because of their valuable genetic characteristics. Retaining the two animals was intended to help preserve genetic diversity and support future breeding efforts.The programme brought together captive breeding expertise from Aussie Ark and scientific research from UTS, with the aim of developing a practical method for returning captive-bred reptiles to their natural habitat.Artificial rocks provide specially designed sheltersOne of the most unusual elements of the experiment is the use of artificial sandstone structures developed to replicate the natural rocky shelters required by broad-headed snakes.The structures were developed by Dr Benjamin Croak, whose research at UTS focused on designing artificial habitats with suitable thermal and physical conditions. They contain crevices where snakes can shelter, regulate their body temperatures and remain protected during daylight hours.The structures also help recreate the conditions in which the reptiles encounter their prey. Since broad-headed snakes hunt smaller rock-dwelling reptiles, suitable habitat is essential for their ability to find food after release.The artificial shelters were placed in restored rocky habitat before the six juvenile snakes were introduced. The approach addresses a major challenge in wildlife reintroduction: breeding animals in captivity is only one part of conservation, as released individuals also need suitable conditions to survive outside controlled environments.Researchers monitor the snakes every fortnightFollowing the May release, Professor Webb's research team and Indigenous rangers began conducting field surveys every two weeks to check the animals' survival and adaptation to their surroundings.The researchers use individual head markings to identify the released snakes and distinguish them during monitoring. This allows the team to track individual animals rather than relying solely on general sightings of the species.An earlier update published on October 1 reported that three of the six snakes had been confirmed alive. The November 6 announcement from UTS raised the number to at least four.One particularly encouraging observation involved a juvenile snake found with a noticeably swollen belly, suggesting it had recently eaten. Conservation ranger Dylan Wallis said the observation indicated that the animal was finding food in its new environment.The monitoring programme is designed to establish whether the snakes can locate prey, use the artificial shelters and survive the challenges of their natural habitat.Indigenous rangers participate in the conservation effortTraditional Owners and Indigenous rangers from the Shoalhaven region are also involved in the reintroduction programme. Their participation includes field monitoring, habitat protection and developing local knowledge of the species.Rangers Ashley Thomas and Dylan Wallis have been associated with the conservation work, while Traditional Owner Frank Connolly Jr. has highlighted the importance of passing environmental knowledge and cultural connections to younger generations.The partnership gives local Indigenous communities an active role in protecting a threatened species on Country. It also supports the development of long-term conservation skills among rangers who can contribute to monitoring and habitat management.Scientists plan further releases and habitat restorationThe six-snake release is an experimental step towards establishing a sustainable wild population. Researchers intend to continue monitoring the animals to understand their long-term survival, feeding behaviour and ability to adapt to the environment.Aussie Ark also plans to continue its captive breeding work, while conservationists explore opportunities to restore additional rocky habitats suitable for future releases.Professor Webb's long-term research, which spans more than three decades, is helping scientists understand the species' ecological requirements and the conditions needed for successful reintroduction.The broader objective is to establish populations capable of surviving and reproducing naturally, reducing their dependence on continued human intervention.You use AI every day. articles.title: Chili's sold nearly 30 million margaritas last year — and a $6 favorite stands out
articles.summary: Chili's sold nearly 30 million margaritas in 2025 and is expanding its drink lineup with premium pours and a Margarita of the Month Club.
articles.body: Chili's dominated restaurant chains in margarita sales in 2025 and is set to sell even more this year as the company finds new ways to keep its signature drink program fresh, according to a new report. The chain sold nearly 30 million margaritas in 2025 and says that many customers come in specifically for the drinks, Nation's Restaurant News recently reported. "Guests are coming to Chili’s for 'margs,'" Mary Ellen Scott, Chili's senior marketing director, told NRN. "It’s part of who we are and part of the experience." CHILI'S GOES VIRAL AFTER ROASTING FAST-FOOD PRICES: 'WHY LET THEM PLAY YOU LIKE THIS?' Frozen margaritas have been a Chili's menu staple since 1975, back when they cost just $1.50, and the chain has revamped the offering in recent years. Frozen drinks now account for 25% of its margarita sales. Last year, Chili's launched a line of premium-liquor frozen margaritas and in February, it introduced a Margarita of the Month Club that allows customers to track how many of the drinks they bought and buy related merch, which is available for anyone to buy. CHILI'S REVIVES ICONIC RED BOOTHS AND CLASSIC DESIGN IN NATIONWIDE RESTAURANT OVERHAUL Customers can collect a digital badge for each month’s margarita and Scott says the "diehard" fans are eager to collect them all. The club builds on the rotating Margarita of the Month program Chili's introduced in 2018, which draws customers in part for its low price of $6. BABY BOOMERS CROWN THEIR FAVORITE CASUAL DINING CHAIN AS GEN Z CHOOSES A DIFFERENT WINNER "It’s value, newness and fun," Scott told NRN. "It's always $6, the drink is changing every month, and we're always looking for ways to make the experience more fun, whether it's a candy or a swizzle." Examples include October’s Witches Brew, a green drink made with Lunazul Blanco Tequila, blue Curaçao, and Monin Granny Smith Apple Syrup served with a broomstick "swizzle," or decorative stirrer. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER November’s StrawEddy Marg combines the tequila with Deep Eddy Lemon Vodka, strawberry purée and house-made sour. The premium-pour margs go for $10 to $12, which is still a steal when cocktails in many major cities are going for around $20. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS The chain also has a full bar, but Scott says the margaritas remain its "flagship." Fox News Digital has reached out to Chili's for comment. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Chili's margaritas made headlines last month for an unrelated safety incident in which North Carolina health officials said a cleaning chemical was mistakenly used to prepare drinks at a Forest City location, causing chemical burns to three customers. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Chili’s said guests and team members were injured and that it is investigating. The restaurant’s permit was briefly suspended, then reinstated.

articles.body: Each reading is based on a fixed rashi tarot anchor and a six-card daily spread covering overall energy, love, career, money, health, and spiritual guidance.MESHA RASHI / ARIESToday's Theme:Clear confidence lifts your day, but patience matters where emotions and egos get tested.Best Area:Health improves through recovery, steadier habits, and a lighter mental load.Watch Out For:Workplace arguments can drain momentum if you react before thinking things through.Card Reading:The Emperor anchors Mesha Rashi, while today's overall card, The Sun upright, warms that structured fire with confidence, visibility, and clean momentum. Leadership feels easier when you stay open, cheerful, and less reactive than usual.General | Card: The Sun uprightToday feels brighter and more straightforward than recent days. The Sun upright puts a strong light on what is working, so don't waste energy doubting yourself or waiting for perfect timing. This is a good day to move with confidence, especially after your morning chai or during an important follow-up. People notice your clarity, but they also notice tone. Stay warm, not forceful. Progress comes faster when you keep things simple, answer directly, and allow one happy moment to reset your mood before the next task.Love and Relationship | Card: Seven of Pentacles reversedLove needs patience more than proof today. With Seven of Pentacles reversed, you may feel you've been waiting too long for a reply, effort, or emotional consistency. Don't turn one delayed WhatsApp reply into a full story. If you're partnered, avoid counting who did more. If you're single, stop checking whether every interaction is leading somewhere immediately. The heart is asking for steadiness, not scorekeeping. A calm conversation will do more than a dramatic reaction, especially if frustration has been building quietly.Education and Career | Card: Five of Swords uprightWork can get sharp quickly, and Five of Swords upright points to ego clashes, competitive behaviour, or one unnecessary argument. Someone may want to win the point instead of solving the issue. Keep your side clean. During a boss follow-up or team discussion, choose facts over attitude. You don't need to prove strength by pushing harder. If a matter feels unfair, document it and step back before responding. The smartest move today is not silence, but measured speech that protects your position without creating fresh friction.Money and Finance | Card: Four of Swords uprightMoney matters benefit from a pause. Four of Swords upright is better for reviewing than rushing, especially around a pending payment, bill, or purchase you've been postponing. Hold off on impulsive spending just because the mood feels good. Check what can wait, what needs one clean transfer, and what should be revisited after a little thought. If a UPI payment or account detail needs confirming, do it carefully. A quiet financial reset today can reduce pressure later in the week.Health and Well-being | Card: Ten of Swords reversedYour energy can improve if you stop treating recovery like laziness. Ten of Swords reversed suggests you're coming out of a tiring phase, especially mentally. Sleep, screen breaks, and lighter food will help more than pushing through. If you've been carrying stress in your body, don't ignore the signs. Slow improvement is still improvement. Let your system catch up.Spiritual Guidance | Card: Seven of Cups reversedSeven of Cups reversed clears mental fog and helps you return to one honest priority. You don't need ten intentions right now. Stand near your prayer corner for a minute and choose one thought to keep, one to release.VRISHABHA RASHI / TAURUSToday's Theme:Relief begins when you stop carrying every worry alone and return to simple grounding.Best Area:Spiritual space feels strong, complete, and quietly reassuring today.Watch Out For:Don't mix gossip, loneliness, and assumptions in close relationships today.Card Reading:The Hierophant anchors Vrishabha Rashi, while today's overall card, Nine of Swords reversed, softens heavy thinking through support, perspective, and recovery. Stability returns when you loosen silent worry and allow relief to enter gradually.General | Card: Nine of Swords reversedA tight mental knot starts loosening today. Nine of Swords reversed suggests worries may not vanish at once, but they don't need to run the whole day either. If you've been replaying the same concern since last night, pause and bring yourself back to what is actually in front of you. A practical routine helps more than more thinking. Read the bank message, answer the one pending task, eat on time, and keep your pace steady. Relief grows through ordinary actions, not dramatic breakthroughs. Let your nervous system trust small calm moments again.Love and Relationship | Card: Three of Cups reversedRelationships can feel socially awkward or emotionally off if too many outside voices are involved. Three of Cups reversed hints at gossip, mixed company, or feeling left out even when people are around. If something from a WhatsApp family group or a casual comment has bothered you, don't let it grow in silence. Speak directly, but gently. Couples should avoid comparing their bond with others. Singles may prefer privacy over noisy attention today. Real closeness won't come from performance. It comes from honesty without extra audience.Education and Career | Card: Seven of Pentacles reversedEffort may feel thankless, and Seven of Pentacles reversed can make you question whether your work is worth the wait. That frustration is real, but don't throw away slow progress just because results aren't immediate. If you're studying, revise your study timetable instead of doubting your ability. At work, check whether you're repeating a method that isn't giving enough return. One adjustment is better than full discouragement. Keep expectations realistic today. Results may be delayed, but useful learning is not wasted.Money and Finance | Card: Nine of Pentacles reversedMoney needs restraint, especially around image-based spending or comfort purchases. With Nine of Pentacles reversed, there can be a temptation to act more secure than you feel, or to overcompensate through online shopping. Before adding anything to the cart, ask whether it's useful this week. Review one recurring expense, one subscription renewal, and one personal indulgence. Financial steadiness comes from small corrections today, not from proving independence through spending.Health and Well-being | Card: Four of Cups reversedEnergy improves when emotional heaviness is acknowledged instead of suppressed. Four of Cups reversed suggests motivation is returning, but gently. If you've been dull, disconnected, or irregular with meals, this is a good day to re-enter routine. Hydration, a proper lunch, and less passive scrolling will help your mood settle. Start small and stay consistent.Spiritual Guidance | Card: The World uprightThe World upright gives a sense of inner completion. Something you've been learning about yourself is ready to settle into wisdom, not struggle. A short temple visit or a few quiet breaths can help you feel that wholeness. What chapter are you ready to consider complete within yourself?MITHUNA RASHI / GEMINIToday's Theme:One draining cycle ends, but clarity depends on choosing fewer words and fewer options.Best Area:Money flows best through traditional planning, advice, and disciplined decisions.Watch Out For:Don't stay stuck in romantic limbo or career fantasies without real action.Card Reading:The Lovers anchors Mithuna Rashi, while today's overall card, Ten of Swords upright, marks a hard stop that exposes what can no longer continue. Clear choices matter more than clever explanations or keeping every option alive.General | Card: Ten of Swords uprightSomething reaches its limit today, and pretending otherwise will only make it heavier. Ten of Swords upright can feel blunt, but it is also clarifying. A plan, conversation, or expectation may show you exactly where it has run out of energy. Let that truth help you simplify. During the commute or between back to back messages, don't fill the silence with overthinking. Cut one draining loop. The day gets better once you stop trying to rescue what's already done. Closure isn't failure here, it's space opening for cleaner choices next.Love and Relationship | Card: The Hanged Man reversedLove feels suspended if no one is willing to move honestly. Pauses become draining when they are used to avoid clarity.Education and Career | Card: Seven of Cups uprightWork and studies can scatter your attention in too many directions. Your mind is quick, but today it needs boundaries. Clear work beats exciting confusion.Money and Finance | Card: The Hierophant uprightMoney improves through simple, traditional handling. The Hierophant upright favours budgeting, trusted advice, and proper systems over experimental spending. Pay attention to due dates, documentation, and one fixed commitment such as rent or EMI. If an elder, mentor, or experienced colleague gives practical guidance, listen before dismissing it. This isn't the day for random financial moves. Stability comes from doing the basic things properly and on time.Health and Well-being | Card: Ten of Pentacles reversedYour body may be reacting to family tension, irregular meals, or a home routine that has gone off track. Ten of Pentacles reversed suggests wellbeing improves when daily structure improves. Eat proper food instead of patchy snacking, and don't skip rest just because everyone else is busy. Grounding matters more than speed today. A stable routine will calm your nerves.Spiritual Guidance | Card: King of Cups uprightKing of Cups upright steadies the inner weather. Emotional maturity is your practice today, especially when words are easy but sincerity is harder. Offer one quiet thank you at your prayer corner for the calm that still remains within you.KARKA RASHI / CANCERToday's Theme:Recognition grows when you stay steady, but private emotions still need honest handling.Best Area:General momentum feels encouraging, and your efforts are likely to be noticed.Watch Out For:Don't avoid one needed conversation just to keep the peace.Card Reading:The Chariot is your anchor, while today's overall card, Six of Wands upright, turns inner determination into visible progress. Let results speak, then move to the next task.Love and Relationship | Card: Two of Swords uprightSomething in relationships is sitting at a pause, and Two of Swords upright points to feelings that are present but not fully spoken. Review any pending payment with a practical eye instead of sentimental hesitation. If someone owes you or expects support, keep boundaries clear and kind. This is also a good day to rethink repeat expenses that no longer fit your present reality. Forward movement begins when your financial choices reflect current priorities, not old patterns.Health and Well-being | Card: Five of Pentacles uprightEnergy can dip if you keep everything to yourself. Five of Pentacles upright often reflects feeling unsupported, and that can show up as low motivation, irregular meals, or emotional tiredness. Keep your body routine simple today. Eat on time, drink enough water, and don't isolate just because your mood shifts. Rest is useful, but withdrawal may make things feel heavier. Reach out if you need practical help.Spiritual Guidance | Card: Queen of Pentacles reversedQueen of Pentacles reversed reminds you that care begins at home, and that includes caring for yourself without guilt. If daily duties have swallowed your inner space, return to one grounding ritual. Sit for two quiet minutes near your prayer corner and notice where you've been overgiving.SIMHA RASHI / LEOToday's Theme:A satisfying milestone is close, and strong partnerships help you complete what matters.Best Area:Career flows best through cooperation, trust, and equal effort today.Watch Out For:Don't push your body past its limit just to keep momentum.Card Reading:Strength is your anchor, while today's overall card, The World upright, brings completion to your efforts. This combination blends heart, stamina, and maturity, making the day feel rewarding when confidence is matched with follow-through.General | Card: The World uprightThere's a sense of completion around you today, and The World upright points to a milestone, a finished cycle, or the relief of seeing something come together properly. Enjoy the progress, but stay grounded enough to close the loop fully.Love and Relationship | Card: The Magician uprightYour charm is high, but The Magician upright works best when confidence stays sincere. Sudden irritation is also a signal. Reset your pace, reduce stimulation, and give yourself recovery time tonight.Spiritual Guidance | Card: Seven of Wands uprightSeven of Wands upright reminds you that inner peace also needs boundaries. articles.title: Australia releases 6 captive-bred broad-headed snakes into the wild in a world first, after building a breeding population from just 17 wild-sourced adults
articles.summary: Endangered broad-headed snake conservation has reached a world first, with captive-bred juveniles released into the wild in Australia.
articles.body: Endangered broad-headed snake conservation has reached a world first, with captive-bred juveniles released into the wild in Australia. The reptile, native only to sandstone escarpments around the Sydney Basin, faces serious decline, yet a breeding programme in New South Wales that began with just 17 wild-sourced adults has now returned six young snakes to their natural rocky habitat. The release involved the University of Technology Sydney and Traditional Landowners of the Shoalhaven, and it follows two years of world-first milestones. The outcome gives conservationists a working model for protecting one of the country’s rarest reptiles while shelter sites keep disappearing.Inside the specialist terrariums where the world’s first captive birth of the species took placeAccording to Aussie Ark’s announcement of the release, the conservation organisation secured the founding adults in October 2024 to create the world’s first wild-sourced breeding and rewilding programme for the species. The insurance population later grew to 20 snakes, all housed in specialised terrariums at Conservation Ark in Somersby, New South Wales.Early in 2026, the programme recorded the world’s first captive birth of the species. Only weeks later, remote-sensor cameras captured a live birth, something never witnessed or documented before. By the time of the May 2026 announcement, eight juveniles had been bred. Two stayed in the insurance population because of their important genetics, and the other six went into the wild.Why artificial rocks matter for a nocturnal snake that has lost so many natural hiding placesThe broad-headed snake shelters under rocks by day and hunts at night. Habitat destruction, illegal rock removal and fragmentation have stripped away the shelter sites it depends on. Professor Jonathan Webb, who has studied the species for more than three decades, said habitat loss remains the greatest threat to its survival.Webb explained that the rocks let the snakes regulate their body temperature and hide, and that they also attract prey. Much of that habitat has been cleared over the decades for landscaping and building. He described the pilot programme using artificial rocks as vital to the snakes’ survival. All six juveniles were released beneath specially designed artificial rocks. Each snake carries a unique marking on its head, so the team can identify every released animal and monitor it over the long term.Indigenous rangers are being trained and supported to monitor and protect the species on CountryThe programme also trains and supports Indigenous rangers, so that monitoring and protection continue on Country long after the first release. Ranger Ashley Thomas said the work is more than a job: “I love it, it’s not a job for me, it’s a passion of mine.” He described the effort as everyone coming together to do what is best for Country.Traditional Owner Frank Connolly Junior said the broad-headed snake is important to his culture. He added that the programme lets young people learn about it, so the knowledge passes to the next generation.Release day cheers and a holistic conservation model for threatened species across AustraliaProject lead Dylan Wallis and Chief Conservation Officer Hayley Shute released one of the juveniles together, and cheers erupted from the crowd as the snake vanished into its new home. “It was thrilling to watch the snakes zip off into the wild,” Shute said.Aussie Ark Managing Director Tim Faulkner called the moment proud and emotional for everyone involved, saying the team had spent many years navigating red tape to reach it. He described the result as a unique, holistic programme that serves as a model for threatened species conservation across Australia.Major partners Australian Power Equipment and the Sunshine Foundation supported the work. The species is also recognised as a priority threatened species under New South Wales and Commonwealth conservation programmes and legislation.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Ambika Mod: Ceiling is getting higher for South Asian actors
articles.summary: The actress joins the cast of Black Doves for the second season of Netflix's spy thriller.
articles.body:
An overworked junior doctor, an aspiring writer and now a ruthless assassin.

Ambika Mod's TV credits are becoming as diverse as the roles are complex.

The actress broke through as the overwhelmed Shruti in BBC medical drama This Is Going To Hurt in 2022, and gained wide recognition for her starring role as Emma Morley in Netflix's miniseries adaptation of David Nicholls' bestselling novel One Day.

Mod, who joins the cast of Black Doves for the second season of the streamer's spy thriller, tells BBC Newsbeat she is careful about the roles she takes on.

As the daughter of Indian immigrants the 31-year-old, from Hatfield, says a "central tenet" of her work is to "change how South Asian women are seen on-screen and the characters that we are seen in".

She has previously spoken about not having access to the same "privilege" some of her fellow actors do when it comes to roles.

Fans have questioned why she hasn't gone on to appear in as many roles as her One Day co-star Leo Woodall, who's since appeared in major films including Bridget Jones: Mad About the Boy and A24's Anthony Bourdain biopic, Tony.

Addressing this remark, Mod tells Newsbeat she thinks "there's definitely an issue in this industry with systemic racism".

"I think it is really hard for South Asian actors to really push through.

"I feel like the glass ceiling is always getting higher and higher and higher."

A report from the Creative Diversity Network suggested that representation of minority ethnic groups on and off-screen dropped slightly last year, after a few years of improvement.

And similar research from media watchdog Ofcom found people from certain backgrounds are less well-represented across the UK broadcasting industry.

It said "people from minority ethnic groups (across the industry as a whole) only account for 11% of those in senior management roles".

It also found under-representation in creative, production and on-screen roles.

Mod says she doesn't know if on-screen representation is changing, but says she "won't engage" with a role if she thinks its tokenistic or stereotypical.

"I've been very, very lucky in my career so far from very early on to play really complex, meaty roles and to have changed the narrative in many ways," she says.

And when it comes to considering what to take on next, she says she tries to follow advice Dame Emma Thompson once gave her: "There's no such thing as a career, there's only what you do next."

"I'm always just trying to focus on what the new challenging thing is going to be, or cool people that I want to work with," she says.

"And also what's going to be fun, as well."

Her latest role as Laila, a lawless agent of the covert Black Doves, attracted her as it subverted a lot of espionage genre tropes.

The character is introduced in season two to assist Keira Knightley's agent Helen on a mission as the stakes get even higher for those working with the secretive organisation.

Mod says it was "such a good time" working alongside Knightley and getting to do some extreme stunt sequences together.

"Honestly, the main reason I wanted to do it was because of all the stunts," she says.

"It was just so fun to take down an absolutely staggering number of men in every single episode."

The thriller also has a dark humour to it, which aligns well with Mod who often brings a dry wit to her characters.

Her comedic career goes back to when she was about 18, and while studying at Durham University she was part of its sketch comedy group.

Despite having not done stand-up for about five years, she says she would "love" to do more comedy in the future.

"I do sometimes think about going back to it," she reveals.

articles.title: Imposing Emergency a mistake, even Indira came to feel the same: Sonia Gandhi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi has called the decision to impose the Emergency in 1975 a mistake, adding that she
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi has called the decision to impose the Emergency in 1975 a mistake, adding that she believes that her mother-in-law and then PM Indira Gandhi had eventually come to feel the same.Her remarks came in an interview with British daily Guardian ahead of the launch of her memoir "Belonging: A Journey of Love".The newspaper reported that Gandhi has written in her book that "keeping Sanjay (Gandhi) in check could have prevented much of the damage that followed".Rajiv was against Emergency, Sanjay pushed for it: SoniaAccording to The Guardian, Sonia Gandhi recalled crying as she witnessed the demolition of Babri Masjid on TV in Dec 1992. She said she knew then that they faced "a long battle for the secular nation that Mahatma Gandhi, Nehru and their colleagues had striven to build".She accepted that failures of her own party had in part contributed to the rise of BJP and its Hindutva politics, the daily reported. "I think we have been too complacent in many ways. There was a laissez-faire kind of an attitude," she was quoted as saying.Reflecting on the Emergency era, Gandhi said, "I always feel that Mrs (Indira) Gandhi was a democrat at heart. I know that many would laugh at this, but I believe she was never comfortable during the course of the Emergency. I think it sat heavy on her."Sonia said the family was split on the decision to impose the Emergency. Her husband Rajiv Gandhi was against the move, telling his mother to wait for the next election, but her younger son Sanjay pushed for it.In another interview published in The Hindu Saturday, Sonia said, "It was not only Sanjay, though in the public mind he is often seen as synonymous with the Emergency. There was a lot of pressure from some of her senior colleagues, and I think there were very few people around her like Rajiv who had a different point of view. I think eventually my mother-in-law began to understand the situation through her own wisdom and took actions to remedy it. "It was only after the Emergency that I came to know about the true gravity of what had been happening. Yes, democratic rights had been curtailed, and there was a suspension of habeas corpus, but it was done constitutionally," the former Congress chief said."Yet, when I take myself back to that period and try and see it from Mrs Gandhi's point of view, I see her struggling to cope with the rapidly deteriorating prevailing circumstances..." Gandhi said. "Hindsight allows us to put things in perspective." Sonia said the former PM had later publicly expressed regret and apologised for excesses during the Emergency.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Alabama finally puts it all together, dominates LSU and leaves Lane Kiffin staring at $40 million CFP disaster
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin fell to 0-6 against Alabama as head coach after the Crimson Tide defense held LSU to one touchdown on four red zone possessions.
articles.body: Alabama spent the past five days taking heat from across the country over its No. 5 ranking in the initial College Football Playoff poll released Tuesday. On Saturday, Kalen DeBoer’s Crimson Tide took out its frustration on Lane Kiffin and LSU in front of a stunned crowd in Baton Rouge, delivering a result that could have major ramifications for the Tigers’ playoff hopes. We all spent the past week arguing over why the Tide would be ranked eight spots ahead of No. 13 Tennessee after the Vols won the head-to-head matchup last month in Knoxville. COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RANKINGS: MIAMI TAKES TOP SPOT, INDIANA CRACKS TOP FIVE IN FIRST OFFICIAL RELEASE The nonstop chatter around Alabama struggling to find an identity behind head coach Kalen DeBoer had become a hot-button topic around college football, while LSU fans were under the impression that Lane Kiffin was turning a corner in the Bayou. Boy, how quickly the tables have turned. LSU spent more than $40 million building its roster this season, acquiring a group of stars through the transfer portal. Now, the Tigers enter the second weekend of November with three losses and their CFP hopes hanging by a thread. On the other side of the field, not worried about Kevin Costner or other celebrities making the walk into a game alongside the head coach, Kalen Deboer has now finally pieced it all together for a squad that has the talent to compete for a national championship. This is the Alabama team the CFP committee thought should be ranked 5th in the country, and the Tide backed up their thinking in a dominant second half way in Baton Rouge. Where did this Alabama performance come from? It's been bubbling Maybe it was the return of Ryan Coleman-Williams or multiple starters on both sides of the ball, but Alabama finally looked like the type of team we thought would grace our television screens on a weekly basis without the hiccups. In front of over 100,000 fans inside Tiger Stadium, it was Alabama's Keelon Russell who fully came out of his shell in what will turn out to be a massive game in terms of his team making the playoff. Three touchdowns and over 200 yards passing, offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb provided his freshman quarterback with the ammunition needed to put Alabama in a spot to win this game. But, winning 31-13 in "Death Valley"? LANE KIFFIN FUMES OVER ALABAMA KICKOFF TIME, ACCUSES SEC OF NOT WANTING LSU TO WIN That's a massive slice of humble-pie served up to Lane Kiffin, and the ones that doubted the heart of this Alabama football team, by a Crimson Tide defense that held LSU to just one touchdown on four redzone possessions. Sure, LSU was moving the ball on offense, but that did not translate to points in Alabama's bend but don't break mindset that had Lane Kiffin shrugging his arms in frustration along the sidelines throughout the third and fourth quarter. On the other hand, Alabama scoring 21 unanswered points put the final nail in this LSU football team that will host a much better looking Texas Longhorns squad next week in Baton Rouge. LSU still has a path to CFP? It's hanging on by a thread with Texas incoming Sure, the Tigers could upset Steve Sarkisian's football team, but there was nothing from the LSU offense that should give fans hope that they can hold up against a Texas defense that will get even healthier over the next week. Obviously, this is the type of scenario that LSU fans were not expecting. The noise that comes with Lane Kiffin is just that — noise. Yes, the Tigers were good enough to have us all wondering how this game would turn out during the third quarter. Fifteen minutes later, Kiffin's record against Alabama as a head coach was 0-6. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Olivia Dunne and Paul Skenes walking with Lane Kiffin through the Tiger Walk makes for some fantastic social media content. But following that up by getting beaten in the trenches by an Alabama team that has been dissected all week for its flaws will not go over well in Baton Rouge. A massive statement was made by Alabama on Saturday night during a week in which the entire country questioned just how good they actually were. Now, everyone should be worried about what this Kalen DeBoer team can do over the next few weeks leading up to selection Sunday in the college football playoff.
